Program Highlights
The Coulter Department's Joint Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering is a collaborative, full-time doctoral program integrating engineering, biology, and medicine. Students are jointly enrolled at Georgia Tech and Emory University, gaining access to exceptional resources across both institutions. The program prepares graduates to lead in academia, industry, or clinical innovation through original research, translational impact, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Program Details
Program Structure
Full-time doctoral program (5–6 years).
Jointly awarded Ph.D. degree from Georgia Tech and Emory University.
Integrated curriculum combining life sciences, engineering, and mathematics.
Team-taught courses by faculty from both institutions.
Problem-based learning in the first year.
Thesis advisor and co-advisor assigned in the first semester.
Dissertation defense expected within five years.
Credit Hours & Requirements
Core courses in life sciences and engineering (Year 1).
Bioethics course and teaching practicum.
Minimum of 9 credit hours of technical electives.
9-credit hour minor outside the thesis research area.

Ph.D. students may specialize in areas such as:
Neural Engineering
Regenerative Medicine
Biomedical Imaging
Computational Biology
Cancer Technologies
Cardiovascular Technologies
Immunoengineering
Health Equity
Biomedical Robotics
Synthetic Biology
Engineering Education
Research Training
Lab rotations and advisor matching in year one.
Emphasis on original, publishable research.
Strong mentorship and interdisciplinary labs.
